newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon MPs demand grace period for media outlets.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon MPs demand grace period for media outlets.

text.p: Ten Lebanese MPs on Tuesday sent an urgent draft law to parliament demanding a five-month grace period for the mass of private television and radio stations ordered to shut down by November 30.
The draft said the stations must be allowed to broadcast news bulletins and political programmes during the grace period ending on April 30, 1997.

In September the government licensed four private television stations -- three of them owned or controlled by politicians -- and 11 private radio stations. Scores were told to close by the end of this month and barred from broadcasting news meanwhile.
The deputies said in the draft that the government's decision created a "grave political crisis...and raised questions about public and media freedoms".
The MPs, seven opposition politicians and three pro-government, said the stations should be allowed to submit new applications to the Information Ministry for licencing or to be allowed to merge.
Several of the media outlets were militia mouthpieces during the 1975-90 civil war but have turned commercial since.
